reuse.why: The API consumer reuses getScheduledAmount, existing consumers share getWorstCaseAmount, and approximate amounts reuse getApproxNumberThreshold.

duplication.why: The change replaces repeated amount-selection logic with one shared implementation without introducing substantial duplicated blocks.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy stays in shared/schedules.ts, while API mapping, forecasting, budgeting, and presentation remain in their existing layers.

scope.why: The edits are focused on expected schedule amounts, their consumers, and related tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralized policy simplifies future changes, although the optional string operator after a positional boolean makes getScheduledAmount less explicit to use.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Changed amount consumers use getScheduledAmount or its shared getWorstCaseAmount implementation.

disguised_duplication.where: Previously repeated amount calculations are removed and routed through shared functions rather than reshaped into new copies.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an operator parameter, and getWorstCaseAmount adds the domain-required isapprox branch using the existing tolerance helper; no changed consumer reimplements the policy.
